diagram_math_checks.result: D has exactly vertices s,u,v,t and arcs s->u, u->v, v->t, with s != t. These three right-pointing arcs appear in the native output. No arc enters s or leaves t. This is an allowed input to step 2.2 and a Hamiltonian ordering under the local Hamiltonian definition.

Step 2.2 replaces u and v by u1-u2-u3 and v1-v2-v3, keeps s3 and t1, and sends the three arcs to s3-u1, u3-v1, v3-t1. Thus G' has precisely eight vertices and seven undirected edges: s3-u1, u1-u2, u2-u3, u3-v1, v1-v2, v2-v3, v3-t1. All seven are visible in the standalone native PNG and present as seven horizontal segments in the compiled SVG. Heavy top arc u->v corresponds exactly to heavy lower edge u3-v1.

Independent local adjacency enumeration gives degree(s3)=degree(t1)=1 and degree 2 for u1,u2,u3,v1,v2,v3. A DFS over that adjacency data found exactly one Hamiltonian path from s3 to t1: s3,u1,u2,u3,v1,v2,v3,t1. It contracts to s,u,v,t. Native SVG has three top edge segments plus three right arrowheads and seven lower edge segments without arrowheads; it has no closing edge t1-s3. All vertices and edge segments checked individually in the standalone original-resolution preview.

The example is explicitly restricted to s != t and a directed path input. It asserts no general graph degree restriction beyond the example; the separate s=t case remains in unchanged step 2.2. Original Statement, Facts and all seven proof steps remain byte-identical and the argument does not cite or rely on the diagram.
